"content" : "# UML class diagram:\nmodel BankAccount\n\nclass Bank\nattributes\n    country:String\n    name:String\n    bic:String\nend\n\nclass Account\nattributes\n    iban: String\n    balance : Integer\nend\n\nclass Person\nattributes\n    firstName:String\n    lastName:String\n    age : Integer\nend\n\nassociation Ownership between\n    Person [1..2] role owner\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nassociation Use between\n    Person [*] role user\n    Account [*]\nend\n\ncomposition AccountOfBanks between\n    Bank [1] role bank\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nconstraints\ncontext Account inv AdultOwners:\n    self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)\n\t\ncontext Account inv positiveBalance:\n    self.balance >= 0\n\n# Syntax example of instances creation:\n-- This is a comment example\n\n-- Primitive data types:\n    -- Integer i.e. 1, 2, 3, etc.\n    -- Real i.e. 1.0, 21.89, 322.05556, etc.\n    -- Boolean i.e. true or false\n    -- String i.e. 'Hello World'\n\n-- You can create instances with the following syntax:\n!new <instance type>('<instance name>')\n-- Example:\n!new Client('client1')\n!new Store('store4')\n\n-- You can assign values to attributes for a created instance with the following syntax:\n!<instance name>.<attribute name> := <value>\n-- Example for different data types:\n!client1.clientId := 1 -- For Integer\n!client1.balance := 1123.45 -- For Real\n!client1.name := 'John' -- For Strings\n!store4.available := true -- For Boolean\n\n-- You can create associations between instances with the following syntax:\n!insert (<instance name1>, <instance name2>) into <association name>\n-- Example:\n!insert (client1, store4) into ClientStore\n\n-- Custom data types usage:\n    -- dataType Location\n    -- operations\n    --   Location(x : Real, y : Real)\n    --   some other operations\n    -- end\n-- You can create custom data types by calling the constructor directly; "content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. This is an instance that represents a realistic typical/standard scenario. Ensure every class and relationship is present in the instance at least once.\n\n"

n{"id":"gen-1771762460-KXcXtgbGhsCkSUv05YdG","provider":"OpenAI","model":"openai/gpt-5.2","object":"chat.completion","created":1771762460,"choices":[{"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","native_finish_reason":"completed","index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"## Edge-case banking instance (unusual but valid)\n\n### Banks\n1) **Bank: “Banque de l’Anse”**\n- **country:** Monaco  \n- **name:** Banque de l’Anse  \n- **bic:** ANSEMC01  \n- **accounts (composition parts):** Account A1, Account A2\n\n2) **Bank: “Kalaallit Banki”**\n- **country:** Greenland  \n- **name:** Kalaallit Banki  \n- **bic:** KALAGLGL  \n- **accounts (composition parts):** *(none)*  \n  - This is the edge case of a bank existing in the model with **zero** accounts, which is allowed (`accounts [0..*]`).\n\n---\n\n### Persons\n1) **Person P1**\n- **firstName:** Noor  \n- **lastName:** El-Masri  \n- **age:** 18  \n- **owns (Ownership.accounts):** Account A1  \n- **uses (Use):** *(none)*\n\n2) **Person P2**\n- **firstName:** Édith  \n- **lastName:** Moreau  \n- **age:** 99  \n- **owns (Ownership.accounts):** Account A1, Account A2  \n- **uses (Use):** *(none)*\n\n3) **Person P3**\n- **firstName:** Luka  \n- **lastName:** Kovač  \n- **age:** 16  \n- **owns (Ownership.accounts):** *(none)*  \n- **uses (Use):** Account A2\n\n4) **Person P4**\n- **firstName:** Anaya  \n- **lastName:** Iyer  \n- **age:** 30  \n- **owns (Ownership.accounts):** *(none)*  \n- **uses (Use):** Account A2\n\n---\n\n### Accounts\n#### Account A1\n- **iban:** DE89370400440532013000  \n- **balance:** 0  *(edge case: exactly at the non-negative lower bound)*  \n- **bank (AccountOfBanks.bank):** Banque de l’Anse (Monaco)\n\n**Ownership (must be 1..2 owners; all owners must be adults):**\n- **owners:**  \n  - Noor El-Masri (age 18) *(edge case: exactly the minimum adult age allowed)*  \n  - Édith Moreau (age 99)  \n- This hits the **maximum** allowed number of owners (**2**), and both owners satisfy `age >= 18`.\n\n**Use (0..* users):**\n- **users:** *(none)*  \n- This is the edge case of an account that has owners but **zero** users, which is permitted.\n\n---\n\n#### Account A2\n- **iban:** FR1420041010050500013M02606  \n- **balance:** 1  *(non-negative; small positive balance)*  \n- **bank (AccountOfBanks.bank):** Banque de l’Anse (Monaco)\n\n**Ownership (must be 1..2 owners; all owners must be adults):**\n- **owners:**  \n  - Édith Moreau (age 99)  \n- This hits the **minimum** allowed number of owners (**1**), satisfying `age >= 18`.\n\n**Use (0..* users):**\n- **users:**  \n  - Luka Kovač (age 16)  \n  - Anaya Iyer (age 30)\n\n**Notable edge behavior (still valid):**\n- Both users of Account A2 are allowed even though one is a **minor (16)**, because the model restricts **owners** to adults but does **not** restrict **users** by age.\n- The **only owner** (Édith Moreau) does **not** use the account at all; the account is used entirely by non-owners, which is unusual but explicitly allowed since Ownership and Use are independent associations.\n\n---\n\n### Constraint check summary\n- **AdultOwners invariant:** Every account owner is age **>= 18** (Noor 18, Édith 99). ✅  \n- **positiveBalance invariant:** Account balances are **>= 0** (A1 = 0, A2 = 1). ✅  \n- **Ownership multiplicity per account:** A1 has 2 owners, A2 has 1 owner (each within **1..2**). ✅  \n- **Bank link per account:** Each account belongs to **exactly 1** bank (both to Banque de l’Anse). ✅  \n- **Banks may have 0..*** accounts: Kalaallit Banki has none. ✅","refusal":null,"reasoning":"**Considering banking scenarios**\n\nI’m working on creating a banking instance that includes banks, accounts, and relationships with constraints. I need to think about unusual yet valid edge cases, like accounts with two owners and a minimum age of 18, while also allowing that a person can use multiple accounts without owning any. I’ll set up Bank A in a tiny country, like Vatican City, and Bank B offshore, with different accounts having specific balance conditions, including zero balances.**Defining banking models**\n\nI’m considering how to define banking models and ensure they’re plausible. Keeping account balances high, like 1,000,000,000, seems safer. I wonder if we can handle IBANs from different countries, even if it's mismatched; it could be an edge case. I need to allow for accounts that have no users, which is an interesting aspect of multiplicity. I'll establish two banks: one with one account and the other with zero accounts, to illustrate ownership and relationships clearly.**Creating banking account structures**\n\nI'm designing a diverse banking structure that includes three accounts. One account in Bank 1 would have two owners and no users. Another account in Bank 1 may have one owner with several users, including minors and non-owners. Bank 2 will remain empty with zero accounts. I’ll include four persons of different ages: someone just turning 18, a 99-year-old, a minor at 16, and an adult at 30. I'll specify the relationships and balances, ensuring some unique configurations.**Defining account ownership and usage**\n\nI’m establishing account ownership details, showing different scenarios. For example, the 30-year-old uses an account but doesn’t own it, while the 18-year-old owns Account X but isn't a user anywhere. The 99-year-old is the owner of both accounts but isn’t a user, except possibly for Account Y where they could use it despite owning none. I'll ensure that all accounts follow the ownership rules with plausible IBAN formats, like using \"SM\" for San Marino, while noting mismatches.**Creating bank structures**\n\nI'm setting up Bank 1 as \"Banque de l'Anse\" in Monaco, with the BIC \"ANSEMC01.\" For Bank 2, I'll name it \" Kalaallit Banki\" in Greenland, using the BIC \"KALAGLGL\" to follow the character requirements. \n\nI'll format IBANs without spaces for clarity — for example, Account X will have the IBAN \"DE89370400440532013000\" with a balance of 0, while Account Y will use \"FR1420041010050500013M02606.\" \n\nIt's essential to highlight that while Bank 1 has accounts, Bank 2 does not, depicting various ownership and usage scenarios within the accounts.","reasoning_details":[{"format":"openai-responses-v1","index":0,"type":"reasoning.summary","summary":"**Considering banking scenarios**\n\nI’m working on creating a banking instance that includes banks, accounts, and relationships with constraints. 13:14:54.793 [Thread-3] INFO  dev.langchain4j.http.client.log.LoggingHttpClient - HTTP request:
- method: POST
- url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions
- headers: [Authorization: Beare...3d], [User-Agent: langchain4j-openai], [Content-Type: application/json]
- body: {
"model" : "openai/gpt-5.2",
"messages" : [ {
"role" : "system",
"content" : "Your task is to generate a complete and diverse instance, in plain English, for a given category and based on a provided conceptual model description. The instance must adhere to these requirements:\n- Be self-contained: Include all required attributes, relationships, and related entities in full detail.\n- Conform to the model: Fulfill the constraints, multiplicities, relationships, and attributes defined in the class diagram model.\n- Understand the context: Ensure that its attributes and relationships are relevant.\n- Avoid duplication of instances: Take into consideration those instances previously built to avoid redundancy.\n- Semantic diversity: From a semantic point of view, incorporate varied scenarios, including regional, linguistic, or cultural differences.\n- Structural diversity: Include instances with different numbers of elements, different numbers of relationships and complexity, and create varied examples by changing entity attributes.\n"
}, {
"role" : "user",
"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. "content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. This is an instance that focuses on the extreme upper or lower limits of valid input ranges. For example:\n- Upper or lower limits of multiplicities.\n- For numbers in a range, the minimum and maximum valid values.\n- Empty collections when possible, i.e., when they do not violate the semantics of the model or its constraints.\n\n"

"role" : "user",
"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. It also enforces basic constraints on account ownership and balances.\n\n### Components\n\n**Class `Bank`**\n- `country: String` — country where the bank is located/registered.\n- `name: String` — bank name.\n- `bic: String` — bank identifier code (BIC/SWIFT).\n\n**Class `Account`**\n- `iban: String` — international bank account number.\n- `balance: Integer` — account balance.\n\n**Class `Person`**\n- `firstName: String` — given name.\n- `lastName: String` — family name.\n- `age: Integer` — age in years.\n\n## Relationships\n\n### 1) Association `Ownership` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [1..2] role owner`\n  - For each **Account**, there must be **at least 1 and at most 2** owning Persons.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Person**, they may own **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n### 2) Association `Use` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [*] role user`\n  - For each **Account**, there may be **0 or more** users.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*]` (no role name given)\n  - For each **Person**, they may use **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n*(Ownership and Use are independent: a person can use an account without owning it, and vice versa.)*\n\n### 3) Composition `AccountOfBanks` (Bank ◼─ Account)\n- **Bank end:** `Bank [1] role bank`\n  - For each **Account**, it is linked to **exactly 1** Bank.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Bank**, it has **0 or more** Accounts.\n- **Composition meaning:** Accounts are treated as parts of a Bank in this model (strong “part-of” relationship).\n\n## Invariants\n\n1) **`AdultOwners` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)`\n- Every owner of an account must be **at least 18 years old**.\n\n2) **`positiveBalance` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.balance >= 0`\n- An account balance must be **non-negative**.\n\n# Category: Overconstraint Detection\nCreate an instance that represents a real-life scenario that is logically valid but violates the model's multiplicities or constraints, exposing overly restrictive or unrealistic restrictions.\n\n"

"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. "content" : "Your task is to generate a complete and diverse instance, in plain English, for a given category and based on a provided conceptual model description. The instance must adhere to these requirements:\n- Be self-contained: Include all required attributes, relationships, and related entities in full detail.\n- Conform to the model: Fulfill the constraints, multiplicities, relationships, and attributes defined in the class diagram model.\n- Understand the context: Ensure that its attributes and relationships are relevant.\n- Avoid duplication of instances: Take into consideration those instances previously built to avoid redundancy.\n- Semantic diversity: From a semantic point of view, incorporate varied scenarios, including regional, linguistic, or cultural differences.\n- Structural diversity: Include instances with different numbers of elements, different numbers of relationships and complexity, and create varied examples by changing entity attributes.\n"
}, {
"role" : "user",
"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. It also enforces basic constraints on account ownership and balances.\n\n### Components\n\n**Class `Bank`**\n- `country: String` — country where the bank is located/registered.\n- `name: String` — bank name.\n- `bic: String` — bank identifier code (BIC/SWIFT).\n\n**Class `Account`**\n- `iban: String` — international bank account number.\n- `balance: Integer` — account balance.\n\n**Class `Person`**\n- `firstName: String` — given name.\n- `lastName: String` — family name.\n- `age: Integer` — age in years.\n\n## Relationships\n\n### 1) Association `Ownership` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [1..2] role owner`\n  - For each **Account**, there must be **at least 1 and at most 2** owning Persons.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Person**, they may own **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n### 2) Association `Use` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [*] role user`\n  - For each **Account**, there may be **0 or more** users.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*]` (no role name given)\n  - For each **Person**, they may use **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n*(Ownership and Use are independent: a person can use an account without owning it, and vice versa.)*\n\n### 3) Composition `AccountOfBanks` (Bank ◼─ Account)\n- **Bank end:** `Bank [1] role bank`\n  - For each **Account**, it is linked to **exactly 1** Bank.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Bank**, it has **0 or more** Accounts.\n- **Composition meaning:** Accounts are treated as parts of a Bank in this model (strong “part-of” relationship).\n\n## Invariants\n\n1) **`AdultOwners` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)`\n- Every owner of an account must be **at least 18 years old**.\n\n2) **`positiveBalance` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.balance >= 0`\n- An account balance must be **non-negative**.\n\n# Category: Overconstraint Detection\nCreate an instance that represents a real-life scenario that is logically valid but violates the model's multiplicities or constraints, exposing overly restrictive or unrealistic restrictions.\n\n"

"role" : "user",
"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. It also enforces basic constraints on account ownership and balances.\n\n### Components\n\n**Class `Bank`**\n- `country: String` — country where the bank is located/registered.\n- `name: String` — bank name.\n- `bic: String` — bank identifier code (BIC/SWIFT).\n\n**Class `Account`**\n- `iban: String` — international bank account number.\n- `balance: Integer` — account balance.\n\n**Class `Person`**\n- `firstName: String` — given name.\n- `lastName: String` — family name.\n- `age: Integer` — age in years.\n\n## Relationships\n\n### 1) Association `Ownership` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [1..2] role owner`\n  - For each **Account**, there must be **at least 1 and at most 2** owning Persons.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Person**, they may own **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n### 2) Association `Use` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [*] role user`\n  - For each **Account**, there may be **0 or more** users.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*]` (no role name given)\n  - For each **Person**, they may use **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n*(Ownership and Use are independent: a person can use an account without owning it, and vice versa.)*\n\n### 3) Composition `AccountOfBanks` (Bank ◼─ Account)\n- **Bank end:** `Bank [1] role bank`\n  - For each **Account**, it is linked to **exactly 1** Bank.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Bank**, it has **0 or more** Accounts.\n- **Composition meaning:** Accounts are treated as parts of a Bank in this model (strong “part-of” relationship).\n\n## Invariants\n\n1) **`AdultOwners` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)`\n- Every owner of an account must be **at least 18 years old**.\n\n2) **`positiveBalance` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.balance >= 0`\n- An account balance must be **non-negative**.\n\n# Category: Baseline Instances\nCreate a baseline instance. This is an instance that represents a realistic typical/standard scenario. Ensure every class and relationship is present in the instance at least once.\n\n"

"role" : "user",
"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. It also enforces basic constraints on account ownership and balances.\n\n### Components\n\n**Class `Bank`**\n- `country: String` — country where the bank is located/registered.\n- `name: String` — bank name.\n- `bic: String` — bank identifier code (BIC/SWIFT).\n\n**Class `Account`**\n- `iban: String` — international bank account number.\n- `balance: Integer` — account balance.\n\n**Class `Person`**\n- `firstName: String` — given name.\n- `lastName: String` — family name.\n- `age: Integer` — age in years.\n\n## Relationships\n\n### 1) Association `Ownership` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [1..2] role owner`\n  - For each **Account**, there must be **at least 1 and at most 2** owning Persons.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Person**, they may own **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n### 2) Association `Use` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [*] role user`\n  - For each **Account**, there may be **0 or more** users.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*]` (no role name given)\n  - For each **Person**, they may use **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n*(Ownership and Use are independent: a person can use an account without owning it, and vice versa.)*\n\n### 3) Composition `AccountOfBanks` (Bank ◼─ Account)\n- **Bank end:** `Bank [1] role bank`\n  - For each **Account**, it is linked to **exactly 1** Bank.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Bank**, it has **0 or more** Accounts.\n- **Composition meaning:** Accounts are treated as parts of a Bank in this model (strong “part-of” relationship).\n\n## Invariants\n\n1) **`AdultOwners` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)`\n- Every owner of an account must be **at least 18 years old**.\n\n2) **`positiveBalance` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.balance >= 0`\n- An account balance must be **non-negative**.\n\n# Category: Complex Instances\nCreate a complex instance that is realistic and contains multiple interrelated entities and/or entities that are involved in multiple constraints.\n\n"

in this case, the constructor of Location requires two arguments: x and y of type Real. So it can be used as follows:\n!store4.location := Location(14.0, 289.0)\n\n-- Enums usage:\n    -- enum Type { Clothes, Shoes }\n-- Can be used as follows:\n!store4.type := #Clothes\n\n# Instance description:\nPlease create the instance according to this specification:\n## Baseline banking instance (typical scenario)\n\n### Bank\n- **Bank B1**\n  - **name:** Nordstadt Bank AG  \n  - **country:** Germany  \n  - **bic:** NDSBDEFFXXX  \n\n### Persons\n- **Person P1**\n  - **firstName:** Anna\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 34\n- **Person P2**\n  - **firstName:** Marco\n  - **lastName:** Rossi\n  - **age:** 41\n- **Person P3**\n  - **firstName:** Sofia\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 17\n\n### Accounts (each account is part of exactly one bank)\n- **Account A1** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00\n  - **balance:** 2450\n- **Account A2** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31\n  - **balance:** 12000\n\n### Ownership relationships (per account: 1 to 2 adult owners)\n- **Account A1 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A1**  \n  *(A1 has exactly 1 owner; owner is an adult.)*\n\n- **Account A2 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi, 41)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  *(A2 has exactly 2 owners; both owners are adults.)*\n\n### Use relationships (independent from ownership; 0 or more users per account)\n- **Users of Account A1:**\n  - **P1 (Anna Müller)** uses **A1** (owner also uses it)\n  - **P3 (Sofia Müller)** uses **A1** (user but **not** an owner)\n\n- **Users of Account A2:**\n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi)** uses **A2** (owner uses it)\n\n### Constraint check (satisfied)\n- **AdultOwners:** All owners (Anna, Marco) are **≥ 18**.  \n- **positiveBalance:** All balances are **≥ 0** (A1 = 2450, A2 = 12000).  \n- **AccountOfBanks composition:** Each account (A1, A2) belongs to **exactly one** bank (B1).\n"

"content" : "# UML class diagram:\nmodel BankAccount\n\nclass Bank\nattributes\n    country:String\n    name:String\n    bic:String\nend\n\nclass Account\nattributes\n    iban: String\n    balance : Integer\nend\n\nclass Person\nattributes\n    firstName:String\n    lastName:String\n    age : Integer\nend\n\nassociation Ownership between\n    Person [1..2] role owner\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nassociation Use between\n    Person [*] role user\n    Account [*]\nend\n\ncomposition AccountOfBanks between\n    Bank [1] role bank\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nconstraints\ncontext Account inv AdultOwners:\n    self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)\n\t\ncontext Account inv positiveBalance:\n    self.balance >= 0\n\n# Syntax example of instances creation:\n-- This is a comment example\n\n-- Primitive data types:\n    -- Integer i.e. 1, 2, 3, etc.\n    -- Real i.e. 1.0, 21.89, 322.05556, etc.\n    -- Boolean i.e. true or false\n    -- String i.e. 'Hello World'\n\n-- You can create instances with the following syntax:\n!new <instance type>('<instance name>')\n-- Example:\n!new Client('client1')\n!new Store('store4')\n\n-- You can assign values to attributes for a created instance with the following syntax:\n!<instance name>.<attribute name> := <value>\n-- Example for different data types:\n!client1.clientId := 1 -- For Integer\n!client1.balance := 1123.45 -- For Real\n!client1.name := 'John' -- For Strings\n!store4.available := true -- For Boolean\n\n-- You can create associations between instances with the following syntax:\n!insert (<instance name1>, <instance name2>) into <association name>\n-- Example:\n!insert (client1, store4) into ClientStore\n\n-- Custom data types usage:\n    -- dataType Location\n    -- operations\n    --   Location(x : Real, y : Real)\n    --   some other operations\n    -- end\n-- You can create custom data types by calling the constructor directly; in this case, the constructor of Location requires two arguments: x and y of type Real. So it can be used as follows:\n!store4.location := Location(14.0, 289.0)\n\n-- Enums usage:\n    -- enum Type { Clothes, Shoes }\n-- Can be used as follows:\n!store4.type := #Clothes\n\n# Instance description:\nPlease create the instance according to this specification:\n## Baseline banking instance (typical scenario)\n\n### Bank\n- **Bank B1**\n  - **name:** Nordstadt Bank AG  \n  - **country:** Germany  \n  - **bic:** NDSBDEFFXXX  \n\n### Persons\n- **Person P1**\n  - **firstName:** Anna\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 34\n- **Person P2**\n  - **firstName:** Marco\n  - **lastName:** Rossi\n  - **age:** 41\n- **Person P3**\n  - **firstName:** Sofia\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 17\n\n### Accounts (each account is part of exactly one bank)\n- **Account A1** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00\n  - **balance:** 2450\n- **Account A2** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31\n  - **balance:** 12000\n\n### Ownership relationships (per account: 1 to 2 adult owners)\n- **Account A1 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A1**  \n  *(A1 has exactly 1 owner; owner is an adult.)*\n\n- **Account A2 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi, 41)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  *(A2 has exactly 2 owners; both owners are adults.)*\n\n### Use relationships (independent from ownership; 0 or more users per account)\n- **Users of Account A1:**\n  - **P1 (Anna Müller)** uses **A1** (owner also uses it)\n  - **P3 (Sofia Müller)** uses **A1** (user but **not** an owner)\n\n- **Users of Account A2:**\n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi)** uses **A2** (owner uses it)\n\n### Constraint check (satisfied)\n- **AdultOwners:** All owners (Anna, Marco) are **≥ 18**.  \n- **positiveBalance:** All balances are **≥ 0** (A1 = 2450, A2 = 12000).  \n- **AccountOfBanks composition:** Each account (A1, A2) belongs to **exactly one** bank (B1).\n"

"messages" : [ {

"content" : "Your task is to generate a complete and diverse instance, in plain English, for a given category and based on a provided conceptual model description. The instance must adhere to these requirements:\n- Be self-contained: Include all required attributes, relationships, and related entities in full detail.\n- Conform to the model: Fulfill the constraints, multiplicities, relationships, and attributes defined in the class diagram model.\n- Understand the context: Ensure that its attributes and relationships are relevant.\n- Avoid duplication of instances: Take into consideration those instances previously built to avoid redundancy.\n- Semantic diversity: From a semantic point of view, incorporate varied scenarios, including regional, linguistic, or cultural differences.\n- Structural diversity: Include instances with different numbers of elements, different numbers of relationships and complexity, and create varied examples by changing entity attributes.\n"
}, {
"role" : "user",
"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. It also enforces basic constraints on account ownership and balances.\n\n### Components\n\n**Class `Bank`**\n- `country: String` — country where the bank is located/registered.\n- `name: String` — bank name.\n- `bic: String` — bank identifier code (BIC/SWIFT).\n\n**Class `Account`**\n- `iban: String` — international bank account number.\n- `balance: Integer` — account balance.\n\n**Class `Person`**\n- `firstName: String` — given name.\n- `lastName: String` — family name.\n- `age: Integer` — age in years.\n\n## Relationships\n\n### 1) Association `Ownership` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [1..2] role owner`\n  - For each **Account**, there must be **at least 1 and at most 2** owning Persons.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Person**, they may own **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n### 2) Association `Use` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [*] role user`\n  - "content" : "# UML class diagram:\nmodel BankAccount\n\nclass Bank\nattributes\n    country:String\n    name:String\n    bic:String\nend\n\nclass Account\nattributes\n    iban: String\n    balance : Integer\nend\n\nclass Person\nattributes\n    firstName:String\n    lastName:String\n    age : Integer\nend\n\nassociation Ownership between\n    Person [1..2] role owner\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nassociation Use between\n    Person [*] role user\n    Account [*]\nend\n\ncomposition AccountOfBanks between\n    Bank [1] role bank\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nconstraints\ncontext Account inv AdultOwners:\n    self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)\n\t\ncontext Account inv positiveBalance:\n    self.balance >= 0\n\n# Syntax example of instances creation:\n-- This is a comment example\n\n-- Primitive data types:\n    -- Integer i.e. 1, 2, 3, etc.\n    -- Real i.e. 1.0, 21.89, 322.05556, etc.\n    -- Boolean i.e. true or false\n    -- String i.e. 'Hello World'\n\n-- You can create instances with the following syntax:\n!new <instance type>('<instance name>')\n-- Example:\n!new Client('client1')\n!new Store('store4')\n\n-- You can assign values to attributes for a created instance with the following syntax:\n!<instance name>.<attribute name> := <value>\n-- Example for different data types:\n!client1.clientId := 1 -- For Integer\n!client1.balance := 1123.45 -- For Real\n!client1.name := 'John' -- For Strings\n!store4.available := true -- For Boolean\n\n-- You can create associations between instances with the following syntax:\n!insert (<instance name1>, <instance name2>) into <association name>\n-- Example:\n!insert (client1, store4) into ClientStore\n\n-- Custom data types usage:\n    -- dataType Location\n    -- operations\n    --   Location(x : Real, y : Real)\n    --   some other operations\n    -- end\n-- You can create custom data types by calling the constructor directly; in this case, the constructor of Location requires two arguments: x and y of type Real. So it can be used as follows:\n!store4.location := Location(14.0, 289.0)\n\n-- Enums usage:\n    -- enum Type { Clothes, Shoes }\n-- Can be used as follows:\n!store4.type := #Clothes\n\n# Instance description:\nPlease create the instance according to this specification:\n## Baseline banking instance (typical scenario)\n\n### Bank\n- **Bank B1**\n  - **name:** Nordstadt Bank AG  \n  - **country:** Germany  \n  - **bic:** NDSBDEFFXXX  \n\n### Persons\n- **Person P1**\n  - **firstName:** Anna\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 34\n- **Person P2**\n  - **firstName:** Marco\n  - **lastName:** Rossi\n  - **age:** 41\n- **Person P3**\n  - **firstName:** Sofia\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 17\n\n### Accounts (each account is part of exactly one bank)\n- **Account A1** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00\n  - **balance:** 2450\n- **Account A2** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31\n  - **balance:** 12000\n\n### Ownership relationships (per account: 1 to 2 adult owners)\n- **Account A1 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A1**  \n  *(A1 has exactly 1 owner; owner is an adult.)*\n\n- **Account A2 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi, 41)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  *(A2 has exactly 2 owners; both owners are adults.)*\n\n### Use relationships (independent from ownership; 0 or more users per account)\n- **Users of Account A1:**\n  - **P1 (Anna Müller)** uses **A1** (owner also uses it)\n  - **P3 (Sofia Müller)** uses **A1** (user but **not** an owner)\n\n- **Users of Account A2:**\n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi)** uses **A2** (owner uses it)\n\n### Constraint check (satisfied)\n- **AdultOwners:** All owners (Anna, Marco) are **≥ 18**.  \n- **positiveBalance:** All balances are **≥ 0** (A1 = 2450, A2 = 12000).  \n- **AccountOfBanks composition:** Each account (A1, A2) belongs to **exactly one** bank (B1).\n"

"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. For each **Account**, there may be **0 or more** users.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*]` (no role name given)\n  - For each **Person**, they may use **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n*(Ownership and Use are independent: a person can use an account without owning it, and vice versa.)*\n\n### 3) Composition `AccountOfBanks` (Bank ◼─ Account)\n- **Bank end:** `Bank [1] role bank`\n  - For each **Account**, it is linked to **exactly 1** Bank.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Bank**, it has **0 or more** Accounts.\n- **Composition meaning:** Accounts are treated as parts of a Bank in this model (strong “part-of” relationship).\n\n## Invariants\n\n1) **`AdultOwners` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)`\n- Every owner of an account must be **at least 18 years old**.\n\n2) **`positiveBalance` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.balance >= 0`\n- An account balance must be **non-negative**.\n\n# Category: Overconstraint Detection\nCreate an instance that represents a real-life scenario that is logically valid but violates the model's multiplicities or constraints, exposing overly restrictive or unrealistic restrictions.\n\n"

"content" : "Your task is to generate a complete and diverse instance, in plain English, for a given category and based on a provided conceptual model description. The instance must adhere to these requirements:\n- Be self-contained: Include all required attributes, relationships, and related entities in full detail.\n- Conform to the model: Fulfill the constraints, multiplicities, relationships, and attributes defined in the class diagram model.\n- Understand the context: Ensure that its attributes and relationships are relevant.\n- Avoid duplication of instances: Take into consideration those instances previously built to avoid redundancy.\n- Semantic diversity: From a semantic point of view, incorporate varied scenarios, including regional, linguistic, or cultural differences.\n- Structural diversity: Include instances with different numbers of elements, different numbers of relationships and complexity, and create varied examples by changing entity attributes.\n"
}, {
"role" : "user",
"content" : "# Conceptual model description:\n## Description\nThe model represents a simple banking domain with **banks**, **accounts**, and **persons**, including who **owns** and **uses** accounts, and which **bank** an account belongs to. It also enforces basic constraints on account ownership and balances.\n\n### Components\n\n**Class `Bank`**\n- `country: String` — country where the bank is located/registered.\n- `name: String` — bank name.\n- `bic: String` — bank identifier code (BIC/SWIFT).\n\n**Class `Account`**\n- `iban: String` — international bank account number.\n- `balance: Integer` — account balance.\n\n**Class `Person`**\n- `firstName: String` — given name.\n- `lastName: String` — family name.\n- `age: Integer` — age in years.\n\n## Relationships\n\n### 1) Association `Ownership` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [1..2] role owner`\n  - For each **Account**, there must be **at least 1 and at most 2** owning Persons.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Person**, they may own **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n### 2) Association `Use` (Person ↔ Account)\n- **Person end:** `Person [*] role user`\n  - For each **Account**, there may be **0 or more** users.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*]` (no role name given)\n  - For each **Person**, they may use **0 or more** Accounts.\n\n*(Ownership and Use are independent: a person can use an account without owning it, and vice versa.)*\n\n### 3) Composition `AccountOfBanks` (Bank ◼─ Account)\n- **Bank end:** `Bank [1] role bank`\n  - For each **Account**, it is linked to **exactly 1** Bank.\n- **Account end:** `Account [*] role accounts`\n  - For each **Bank**, it has **0 or more** Accounts.\n- **Composition meaning:** Accounts are treated as parts of a Bank in this model (strong “part-of” relationship).\n\n## Invariants\n\n1) **`AdultOwners` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)`\n- Every owner of an account must be **at least 18 years old**.\n\n2) **`positiveBalance` (context `Account`)**\n- `self.balance >= 0`\n- An account balance must be **non-negative**.\n\n# Category: Complex Instances\nCreate a complex instance that is realistic and contains multiple interrelated entities and/or entities that are involved in multiple constraints.\n\n"

So it can be used as follows:\n!store4.location := Location(14.0, 289.0)\n\n-- Enums usage:\n    -- enum Type { Clothes, Shoes }\n-- Can be used as follows:\n!store4.type := #Clothes\n\n# Instance description:\nPlease create the instance according to this specification:\n## Baseline banking instance (typical scenario)\n\n### Bank\n- **Bank B1**\n  - **name:** Nordstadt Bank AG  \n  - **country:** Germany  \n  - **bic:** NDSBDEFFXXX  \n\n### Persons\n- **Person P1**\n  - **firstName:** Anna\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 34\n- **Person P2**\n  - **firstName:** Marco\n  - **lastName:** Rossi\n  - **age:** 41\n- **Person P3**\n  - **firstName:** Sofia\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 17\n\n### Accounts (each account is part of exactly one bank)\n- **Account A1** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00\n  - **balance:** 2450\n- **Account A2** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31\n  - **balance:** 12000\n\n### Ownership relationships (per account: 1 to 2 adult owners)\n- **Account A1 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A1**  \n  *(A1 has exactly 1 owner; owner is an adult.)*\n\n- **Account A2 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi, 41)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  *(A2 has exactly 2 owners; both owners are adults.)*\n\n### Use relationships (independent from ownership; 0 or more users per account)\n- **Users of Account A1:**\n  - **P1 (Anna Müller)** uses **A1** (owner also uses it)\n  - **P3 (Sofia Müller)** uses **A1** (user but **not** an owner)\n\n- **Users of Account A2:**\n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi)** uses **A2** (owner uses it)\n\n### Constraint check (satisfied)\n- **AdultOwners:** All owners (Anna, Marco) are **≥ 18**.  \n- **positiveBalance:** All balances are **≥ 0** (A1 = 2450, A2 = 12000).  \n- **AccountOfBanks composition:** Each account (A1, A2) belongs to **exactly one** bank (B1).\n"

"content" : "You are tasked with creating instances of a conceptual model in the UML-based Specification Environment (USE). You will receive:\n1. The UML class diagram that the instance follows.\n2. A sample syntax of instances creation.\n3. A description of the instance that needs to be created.\n\nYour goal is to generate these instances based on the provided description, adhering strictly to these requirements:\n- The output must be in plain text, with no additional comments, descriptions, or explanations.\n- Ensure that the created instance adheres to the provided description.\n- Follow the syntax sample provided, without deviation.\n- Take into account previously created instances to avoid using duplicate naming.\n"
}, {
"role" : "user",
"content" : "# UML class diagram:\nmodel BankAccount\n\nclass Bank\nattributes\n    country:String\n    name:String\n    bic:String\nend\n\nclass Account\nattributes\n    iban: String\n    balance : Integer\nend\n\nclass Person\nattributes\n    firstName:String\n    lastName:String\n    age : Integer\nend\n\nassociation Ownership between\n    Person [1..2] role owner\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nassociation Use between\n    Person [*] role user\n    Account [*]\nend\n\ncomposition AccountOfBanks between\n    Bank [1] role bank\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nconstraints\ncontext Account inv AdultOwners:\n    self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)\n\t\ncontext Account inv positiveBalance:\n    self.balance >= 0\n\n# Syntax example of instances creation:\n-- This is a comment example\n\n-- Primitive data types:\n    -- Integer i.e. 1, 2, 3, etc.\n    -- Real i.e. 1.0, 21.89, 322.05556, etc.\n    -- Boolean i.e. true or false\n    -- String i.e. 'Hello World'\n\n-- You can create instances with the following syntax:\n!new <instance type>('<instance name>')\n-- Example:\n!new Client('client1')\n!new Store('store4')\n\n-- You can assign values to attributes for a created instance with the following syntax:\n!<instance name>.<attribute name> := <value>\n-- Example for different data types:\n!client1.clientId := 1 -- For Integer\n!client1.balance := 1123.45 -- For Real\n!client1.name := 'John' -- For Strings\n!store4.available := true -- For Boolean\n\n-- You can create associations between instances with the following syntax:\n!insert (<instance name1>, <instance name2>) into <association name>\n-- Example:\n!insert (client1, store4) into ClientStore\n\n-- Custom data types usage:\n    -- dataType Location\n    -- operations\n    --   Location(x : Real, y : Real)\n    --   some other operations\n    -- end\n-- You can create custom data types by calling the constructor directly; in this case, the constructor of Location requires two arguments: x and y of type Real. So it can be used as follows:\n!store4.location := Location(14.0, 289.0)\n\n-- Enums usage:\n    -- enum Type { Clothes, Shoes }\n-- Can be used as follows:\n!store4.type := #Clothes\n\n# Instance description:\nPlease create the instance according to this specification:\n## Baseline banking instance (typical scenario)\n\n### Bank\n- **Bank B1**\n  - **name:** Nordstadt Bank AG  \n  - **country:** Germany  \n  - **bic:** NDSBDEFFXXX  \n\n### Persons\n- **Person P1**\n  - **firstName:** Anna\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 34\n- **Person P2**\n  - **firstName:** Marco\n  - **lastName:** Rossi\n  - **age:** 41\n- **Person P3**\n  - **firstName:** Sofia\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 17\n\n### Accounts (each account is part of exactly one bank)\n- **Account A1** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00\n  - **balance:** 2450\n- **Account A2** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31\n  - **balance:** 12000\n\n### Ownership relationships (per account: 1 to 2 adult owners)\n- **Account A1 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A1**  \n  *(A1 has exactly 1 owner; owner is an adult.)*\n\n- **Account A2 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi, 41)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  *(A2 has exactly 2 owners; both owners are adults.)*\n\n### Use relationships (independent from ownership; 0 or more users per account)\n- **Users of Account A1:**\n  - **P1 (Anna Müller)** uses **A1** (owner also uses it)\n  - **P3 (Sofia Müller)** uses **A1** (user but **not** an owner)\n\n- **Users of Account A2:**\n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi)** uses **A2** (owner uses it)\n\n### Constraint check (satisfied)\n- **AdultOwners:** All owners (Anna, Marco) are **≥ 18**.  \n- **positiveBalance:** All balances are **≥ 0** (A1 = 2450, A2 = 12000).  \n- **AccountOfBanks composition:** Each account (A1, A2) belongs to **exactly one** bank (B1).\n"
}, {
"role" : "assistant",
"content" : "!new Bank('b1')\n!b1.name := 'Nordstadt Bank AG'\n!b1.country := 'Germany'\n!b1.bic := 'NDSBDEFFXXX'\n\n!new Person('p1')\n!p1.firstName := 'Anna'\n!p1.lastName := 'Müller'\n!p1.age := 34\n\n!new Person('p2')\n!p2.firstName := 'Marco'\n!p2.lastName := 'Rossi'\n!p2.age := 41\n\n!new Person('p3')\n!p3.firstName := 'Sofia'\n!p3.lastName := 'Müller'\n!p3.age := 17\n\n!new Account('a1')\n!a1.iban := 'DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00'\n!a1.balance := 2450\n\n!new Account('a2')\n!a2.iban := 'DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31'\n!a2.balance := 12000\n\n!insert (b1, a1) into AccountOfBanks\n!insert (b1, a2) into AccountOfBanks\n\n!insert (p1, a1) into Ownership\n!insert (p1, a2) into Ownership\n!insert (p2, a2) into Ownership\n\n!insert (p1, a1) into Use\n!insert (p3, a1) into Use\n!insert (p2, a2) into Use"

So it can be used as follows:\n!store4.location := Location(14.0, 289.0)\n\n-- Enums usage:\n    -- enum Type { Clothes, Shoes }\n-- Can be used as follows:\n!store4.type := #Clothes\n\n# Instance description:\nPlease create the instance according to this specification:\n## Baseline banking instance (typical scenario)\n\n### Bank\n- **Bank B1**\n  - **name:** Nordstadt Bank AG  \n  - **country:** Germany  \n  - **bic:** NDSBDEFFXXX  \n\n### Persons\n- **Person P1**\n  - **firstName:** Anna\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 34\n- **Person P2**\n  - **firstName:** Marco\n  - **lastName:** Rossi\n  - **age:** 41\n- **Person P3**\n  - **firstName:** Sofia\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 17\n\n### Accounts (each account is part of exactly one bank)\n- **Account A1** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00\n  - **balance:** 2450\n- **Account A2** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31\n  - **balance:** 12000\n\n### Ownership relationships (per account: 1 to 2 adult owners)\n- **Account A1 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A1**  \n  *(A1 has exactly 1 owner; owner is an adult.)*\n\n- **Account A2 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi, 41)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  *(A2 has exactly 2 owners; both owners are adults.)*\n\n### Use relationships (independent from ownership; 0 or more users per account)\n- **Users of Account A1:**\n  - **P1 (Anna Müller)** uses **A1** (owner also uses it)\n  - **P3 (Sofia Müller)** uses **A1** (user but **not** an owner)\n\n- **Users of Account A2:**\n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi)** uses **A2** (owner uses it)\n\n### Constraint check (satisfied)\n- **AdultOwners:** All owners (Anna, Marco) are **≥ 18**.  \n- **positiveBalance:** All balances are **≥ 0** (A1 = 2450, A2 = 12000).  \n- **AccountOfBanks composition:** Each account (A1, A2) belongs to **exactly one** bank (B1).\n"

in this case, the constructor of Location requires two arguments: x and y of type Real. in this case, the constructor of Location requires two arguments: x and y of type Real. So it can be used as follows:\n!store4.location := Location(14.0, 289.0)\n\n-- Enums usage:\n    -- enum Type { Clothes, Shoes }\n-- Can be used as follows:\n!store4.type := #Clothes\n\n# Instance description:\nPlease create the instance according to this specification:\n## Baseline banking instance (typical scenario)\n\n### Bank\n- **Bank B1**\n  - **name:** Nordstadt Bank AG  \n  - **country:** Germany  \n  - **bic:** NDSBDEFFXXX  \n\n### Persons\n- **Person P1**\n  - **firstName:** Anna\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 34\n- **Person P2**\n  - **firstName:** Marco\n  - **lastName:** Rossi\n  - **age:** 41\n- **Person P3**\n  - **firstName:** Sofia\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 17\n\n### Accounts (each account is part of exactly one bank)\n- **Account A1** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00\n  - **balance:** 2450\n- **Account A2** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31\n  - **balance:** 12000\n\n### Ownership relationships (per account: 1 to 2 adult owners)\n- **Account A1 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A1**  \n  *(A1 has exactly 1 owner; owner is an adult.)*\n\n- **Account A2 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi, 41)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  *(A2 has exactly 2 owners; both owners are adults.)*\n\n### Use relationships (independent from ownership; 0 or more users per account)\n- **Users of Account A1:**\n  - **P1 (Anna Müller)** uses **A1** (owner also uses it)\n  - **P3 (Sofia Müller)** uses **A1** (user but **not** an owner)\n\n- **Users of Account A2:**\n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi)** uses **A2** (owner uses it)\n\n### Constraint check (satisfied)\n- **AdultOwners:** All owners (Anna, Marco) are **≥ 18**.  \n- **positiveBalance:** All balances are **≥ 0** (A1 = 2450, A2 = 12000).  \n- **AccountOfBanks composition:** Each account (A1, A2) belongs to **exactly one** bank (B1).\n"

"content" : "# UML class diagram:\nmodel BankAccount\n\nclass Bank\nattributes\n    country:String\n    name:String\n    bic:String\nend\n\nclass Account\nattributes\n    iban: String\n    balance : Integer\nend\n\nclass Person\nattributes\n    firstName:String\n    lastName:String\n    age : Integer\nend\n\nassociation Ownership between\n    Person [1..2] role owner\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nassociation Use between\n    Person [*] role user\n    Account [*]\nend\n\ncomposition AccountOfBanks between\n    Bank [1] role bank\n    Account [*] role accounts\nend\n\nconstraints\ncontext Account inv AdultOwners:\n    self.owner->forAll(p | p.age >= 18)\n\t\ncontext Account inv positiveBalance:\n    self.balance >= 0\n\n# Syntax example of instances creation:\n-- This is a comment example\n\n-- Primitive data types:\n    -- Integer i.e. 1, 2, 3, etc.\n    -- Real i.e. 1.0, 21.89, 322.05556, etc.\n    -- Boolean i.e. true or false\n    -- String i.e. 'Hello World'\n\n-- You can create instances with the following syntax:\n!new <instance type>('<instance name>')\n-- Example:\n!new Client('client1')\n!new Store('store4')\n\n-- You can assign values to attributes for a created instance with the following syntax:\n!<instance name>.<attribute name> := <value>\n-- Example for different data types:\n!client1.clientId := 1 -- For Integer\n!client1.balance := 1123.45 -- For Real\n!client1.name := 'John' -- For Strings\n!store4.available := true -- For Boolean\n\n-- You can create associations between instances with the following syntax:\n!insert (<instance name1>, <instance name2>) into <association name>\n-- Example:\n!insert (client1, store4) into ClientStore\n\n-- Custom data types usage:\n    -- dataType Location\n    -- operations\n    --   Location(x : Real, y : Real)\n    --   some other operations\n    -- end\n-- You can create custom data types by calling the constructor directly; in this case, the constructor of Location requires two arguments: x and y of type Real. So it can be used as follows:\n!store4.location := Location(14.0, 289.0)\n\n-- Enums usage:\n    -- enum Type { Clothes, Shoes }\n-- Can be used as follows:\n!store4.type := #Clothes\n\n# Instance description:\nPlease create the instance according to this specification:\n## Baseline banking instance (typical scenario)\n\n### Bank\n- **Bank B1**\n  - **name:** Nordstadt Bank AG  \n  - **country:** Germany  \n  - **bic:** NDSBDEFFXXX  \n\n### Persons\n- **Person P1**\n  - **firstName:** Anna\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 34\n- **Person P2**\n  - **firstName:** Marco\n  - **lastName:** Rossi\n  - **age:** 41\n- **Person P3**\n  - **firstName:** Sofia\n  - **lastName:** Müller\n  - **age:** 17\n\n### Accounts (each account is part of exactly one bank)\n- **Account A1** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00\n  - **balance:** 2450\n- **Account A2** (part of **Bank B1**)\n  - **iban:** DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31\n  - **balance:** 12000\n\n### Ownership relationships (per account: 1 to 2 adult owners)\n- **Account A1 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A1**  \n  *(A1 has exactly 1 owner; owner is an adult.)*\n\n- **Account A2 owners:**  \n  - **P1 (Anna Müller, 34)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi, 41)** is an **owner** of **A2**  \n  *(A2 has exactly 2 owners; both owners are adults.)*\n\n### Use relationships (independent from ownership; 0 or more users per account)\n- **Users of Account A1:**\n  - **P1 (Anna Müller)** uses **A1** (owner also uses it)\n  - **P3 (Sofia Müller)** uses **A1** (user but **not** an owner)\n\n- **Users of Account A2:**\n  - **P2 (Marco Rossi)** uses **A2** (owner uses it)\n\n### Constraint check (satisfied)\n- **AdultOwners:** All owners (Anna, Marco) are **≥ 18**.  \n- **positiveBalance:** All balances are **≥ 0** (A1 = 2450, A2 = 12000).  \n- **AccountOfBanks composition:** Each account (A1, A2) belongs to **exactly one** bank (B1).\n"
}, {

"content" : "!new Bank('b1')\n!b1.name := 'Nordstadt Bank AG'\n!b1.country := 'Germany'\n!b1.bic := 'NDSBDEFFXXX'\n\n!new Person('p1')\n!p1.firstName := 'Anna'\n!p1.lastName := 'Müller'\n!p1.age := 34\n\n!new Person('p2')\n!p2.firstName := 'Marco'\n!p2.lastName := 'Rossi'\n!p2.age := 41\n\n!new Person('p3')\n!p3.firstName := 'Sofia'\n!p3.lastName := 'Müller'\n!p3.age := 17\n\n!new Account('a1')\n!a1.iban := 'DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00'\n!a1.balance := 2450\n\n!new Account('a2')\n!a2.iban := 'DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31'\n!a2.balance := 12000\n\n!insert (b1, a1) into AccountOfBanks\n!insert (b1, a2) into AccountOfBanks\n\n!insert (p1, a1) into Ownership\n!insert (p1, a2) into Ownership\n!insert (p2, a2) into Ownership\n\n!insert (p1, a1) into Use\n!insert (p3, a1) into Use\n!insert (p2, a2) into Use"

"content" : "Continue with the following description, creating the instance according to the syntax example and this specification: \n## Edge-case banking instance (unusual but valid)\n\n### Banks\n1) **Bank: “Banque de l’Anse”**\n- **country:** Monaco  \n- **name:** Banque de l’Anse  \n- **bic:** ANSEMC01  \n- **accounts (composition parts):** Account A1, Account A2\n\n2) **Bank: “Kalaallit Banki”**\n- **country:** Greenland  \n- **name:** Kalaallit Banki  \n- **bic:** KALAGLGL  \n- **accounts (composition parts):** *(none)*  \n  - This is the edge case of a bank existing in the model with **zero** accounts, which is allowed (`accounts [0..*]`).\n\n---\n\n### Persons\n1) **Person P1**\n- **firstName:** Noor  \n- **lastName:** El-Masri  \n- **age:** 18  \n- **owns (Ownership.accounts):** Account A1  \n- **uses (Use):** *(none)*\n\n2) **Person P2**\n- **firstName:** Édith  \n- **lastName:** Moreau  \n- **age:** 99  \n- **owns (Ownership.accounts):** Account A1, Account A2  \n- **uses (Use):** *(none)*\n\n3) **Person P3**\n- **firstName:** Luka  \n- **lastName:** Kovač  \n- **age:** 16  \n- **owns (Ownership.accounts):** *(none)*  \n- **uses (Use):** Account A2\n\n4) **Person P4**\n- **firstName:** Anaya  \n- **lastName:** Iyer  \n- **age:** 30  \n- **owns (Ownership.accounts):** *(none)*  \n- **uses (Use):** Account A2\n\n---\n\n### Accounts\n#### Account A1\n- **iban:** DE89370400440532013000  \n- **balance:** 0  *(edge case: exactly at the non-negative lower bound)*  \n- **bank (AccountOfBanks.bank):** Banque de l’Anse (Monaco)\n\n**Ownership (must be 1..2 owners; all owners must be adults):**\n- **owners:**  \n  - Noor El-Masri (age 18) *(edge case: exactly the minimum adult age allowed)*  \n  - Édith Moreau (age 99)  \n- This hits the **maximum** allowed number of owners (**2**), and both owners satisfy `age >= 18`.\n\n**Use (0..* users):**\n- **users:** *(none)*  \n- This is the edge case of an account that has owners but **zero** users, which is permitted.\n\n---\n\n#### Account A2\n- **iban:** FR1420041010050500013M02606  \n- **balance:** 1  *(non-negative; small positive balance)*  \n- **bank (AccountOfBanks.bank):** Banque de l’Anse (Monaco)\n\n**Ownership (must be 1..2 owners; all owners must be adults):**\n- **owners:**  \n  - Édith Moreau (age 99)  \n- This hits the **minimum** allowed number of owners (**1**), satisfying `age >= 18`.\n\n**Use (0..* users):**\n- **users:**  \n  - Luka Kovač (age 16)  \n  - Anaya Iyer (age 30)\n\n**Notable edge behavior (still valid):**\n- Both users of Account A2 are allowed even though one is a **minor (16)**, because the model restricts **owners** to adults but does **not** restrict **users** by age.\n- The **only owner** (Édith Moreau) does **not** use the account at all; the account is used entirely by non-owners, which is unusual but explicitly allowed since Ownership and Use are independent associations.\n\n---\n\n### Constraint check summary\n- **AdultOwners invariant:** Every account owner is age **>= 18** (Noor 18, Édith 99). ✅  \n- **positiveBalance invariant:** Account balances are **>= 0** (A1 = 0, A2 = 1). ✅  \n- **Ownership multiplicity per account:** A1 has 2 owners, A2 has 1 owner (each within **1..2**). ✅  \n- **Bank link per account:** Each account belongs to **exactly 1** bank (both to Banque de l’Anse). ✅  \n- **Banks may have 0..*** accounts: Kalaallit Banki has none. ✅"
